scenarios.title: Map every building
scenarios.short: Roof outline of every building in your area, as editable polygons.
scenarios.long: Finds building roofs on high-resolution imagery and returns one polygon per building. Objects under 20 m² are dropped to keep the layer clean. Switch on building types, heights or cleaner shapes in the run form.
scenarios.output: A styled polygon layer of building roofs in the Mapflow group.
scenarios.best: Aerial or satellite imagery at 0.3 m per pixel (zoom 19).
uses: Refresh a municipal building layer before a field survey
Count structures in a settlement for planning or emergency response
Find parcels with new or missing buildings
scenarios.costNote: Example: 10 km² on Mapbox zoom 19 ≈ 190 credits. Your own imagery costs nothing.

scenarios.title: Sort buildings by type
scenarios.short: Every building polygon carries a type, ready to filter and style.
scenarios.long: Runs the Buildings model with classification switched on, so each roof polygon gets a building class. Classification adds no extra cost.
scenarios.output: Building polygons with a class attribute.
scenarios.best: Aerial or satellite imagery at 0.3 m per pixel (zoom 19).
uses: Compare residential and non-residential stock by district
Pull industrial and commercial sites into their own layer
Feed zoning and land-use analysis with fresh data
scenarios.costNote: Example: 10 km² on Mapbox zoom 19 ≈ 190 credits.

scenarios.title: Building heights and 3D footprints
scenarios.short: A height for each building, with the outline moved from roof to ground.
scenarios.long: Adds a height model that reads shadow length and visible walls. The result is a 3D footprint: the building contour projected to ground level instead of the roof outline.
scenarios.output: Footprint polygons with a height attribute, ready for the QGIS 3D map view.
scenarios.best: 0.3 m imagery (zoom 19) with visible shadows. Helps most on oblique imagery, where roofs look shifted.
uses: Extrude buildings in the QGIS 3D map view
Estimate floor area and building volume
Screen areas for shade and line-of-sight studies
scenarios.costNote: Example: 10 km² on Mapbox zoom 19 ≈ 290 credits.

scenarios.title: Map forest and tree cover
scenarios.short: All tree and shrub cover, down to small groups and tree lines.
scenarios.long: Segments every area covered by trees and shrubs, including sparse forest and shrubland. It works in most environments, cities included.
scenarios.output: A polygon layer of tree and shrub cover.
scenarios.best: 0.6–0.3 m imagery (zoom 18–19) taken in the growing season. Leafless or snow-covered trees are not detected.
uses: Measure canopy cover per district or parcel
Compare two dates to find cleared forest
Build a green-space inventory for a city
scenarios.costNote: Example: 10 km² on Mapbox zoom 18 ≈ 110 credits.

scenarios.title: Vegetation height along power lines
scenarios.short: Vegetation split into shrubs, 4–10 m forest and forest over 10 m.
scenarios.long: Runs the forest model with height estimation. Vegetation is classed as shrubs under 4 m, forest from 4 to 10 m and forest over 10 m, which is what vegetation managers need near power lines.
scenarios.output: Vegetation polygons with a height class.
scenarios.best: 0.6–0.3 m imagery (zoom 18–19) taken in the growing season.
uses: Prioritise clearance work in power line corridors
Plan right-of-way maintenance by height class
Screen vegetation along roads and railways
scenarios.tip: Buffer your line layer in QGIS (Vector › Geoprocessing › Buffer) and use the buffer as the area, so you pay only for the corridor.
scenarios.costNote: Example: a 10 km² corridor on Mapbox zoom 18 ≈ 210 credits.

scenarios.title: Count individual trees
scenarios.short: A point for every tree crown, free-standing trees included.
scenarios.long: Extracts tree crowns from forest and from single trees, as points with a crown radius or as crown polygons.
scenarios.output: Tree crown points with a radius, or crown polygons.
scenarios.best: 0.3 m imagery (zoom 19) to separate individual trees.
uses: Street-tree and park inventories
Count trees in orchards and plantations
Track tree loss on a construction site
scenarios.costNote: Example: 10 km² on Mapbox zoom 19 ≈ 270 credits.

scenarios.title: Extract the road network
scenarios.short: A connected road network with gaps merged and short stubs removed.
scenarios.long: Finds road centrelines, cleans the graph (simplifies geometry, merges gaps, removes double edges and short detached pieces) and turns it back into road polygons.
scenarios.output: Road polygons built from a cleaned centreline network.
scenarios.best: Rural and suburban areas with 0.3–0.5 m imagery. Dense city centres with wide sidewalks are harder.
uses: Map access roads and tracks for rural planning
Add forestry and field tracks missing from OSM
Check the street network in new suburbs
scenarios.costNote: Example: 10 km² on Mapbox zoom 18 ≈ 80 credits.

scenarios.title: Base map in one run
scenarios.short: Buildings, roads and forest together, with topology corrected.
scenarios.long: Runs the Buildings, Roads and Forest models as one workflow and returns a single topology-corrected result, so the layers do not overlap.
scenarios.output: Buildings, roads and forest from one run, added as separate styled layers.
uses: Start a base map where no vector data exists
Get a land-use overview before a site visit
Create a reference layer for disaster response
scenarios.costNote: Example: 10 km² on Mapbox zoom 18 ≈ 260 credits.

scenarios.title: Get OpenStreetMap and Overture data
scenarios.short: Community map data for your area, with no AI model involved.
scenarios.long: Downloads the classes you choose from OpenStreetMap and Overture Maps for your area, so you can check coverage before running AI, or fill gaps after.
scenarios.output: Vector layers for each class you select.
scenarios.best: Any area. Quality depends on how complete open data is there, and it may not line up exactly with the imagery.
uses: Check OSM completeness before paying for AI mapping
Combine open data with AI results
Add context layers to a project in one step
scenarios.costNote: No AI model is used. You still pick imagery as a visual reference.

scenarios.title: Map your drone or aerial orthophoto
scenarios.short: Run any model on your own GeoTIFF or a raster layer already in QGIS.
scenarios.long: Upload an image to My imagery, or pick a raster layer from your QGIS project, and run any model on it. Collections let you process many images in one go.
scenarios.output: The layers of the model you choose, clipped to the image or your area.
scenarios.best: Georeferenced RGB 8-bit GeoTIFF, up to 1 GB. Check each model’s resolution needs.
uses: Map buildings on a fresh drone survey
Process an orthophoto from a municipal flight
Re-run older imagery to compare with today
scenarios.costNote: Imagery you bring costs 0 credits. Example: 10 km² with Buildings = 100 credits.

apply.hint: Pick a collection from My imagery or upload a GeoTIFF, then choose what to map.

scenarios.title: Find a fresh image, then map it
scenarios.short: Search satellite catalogs by date, cloud and angle, then map the image you pick.
scenarios.long: Searches mosaics and commercial scenes over your area. Mosaics run right away; scenes are ordered through Mapflow Web.
scenarios.output: The layers of the model you choose, on the image you picked.
scenarios.best: Areas that changed recently: new construction, storm or flood damage, seasonal cover.
uses: Map buildings built in the last few months
Check an area after a storm or flood
Pick a cloud-free image for a vegetation survey
scenarios.costNote: Mosaics start at 1 credit per km². Commercial scenes: 60 credits per km² at 0.5 m, 180 at 0.3 m.

apply.hint: Search the catalog over your area and press Use on an image.

scenarios.title: Find solar panels
scenarios.short: Photovoltaic panels on rooftops and on the ground.
scenarios.long: A detection and segmentation model for photovoltaic panels, trained on aerial imagery. It finds panels on rooftops and in solar farms.
uses: Inventory rooftop solar in a municipality
Monitor solar farm build-out
Estimate installed panel area for grid planning
scenarios.costNote: Request access and we connect the model to your account.

scenarios.title: Spot construction sites
scenarios.short: Outlines of construction sites and buildings under construction.
scenarios.long: Outlines areas that contain construction sites and buildings under construction. Available for selected countries; coverage is growing.
scenarios.best: High-resolution satellite imagery of fast-developing areas.
uses: Track new development for permits and taxes
Monitor progress on large projects
Flag unplanned construction
scenarios.costNote: Request access and we connect the model to your account.

scenarios.title: Delineate agricultural fields
scenarios.short: Field boundaries separated by tree lines, roads or crop stage.
scenarios.long: Detects agricultural fields and separates neighbouring fields where a visible boundary exists. Tuned for larger fields in Europe with active vegetation.
scenarios.best: 1–1.2 m imagery in the growing season.
uses: Build field boundaries for farm management
Estimate cultivated area per region
Prepare parcels for crop monitoring
scenarios.costNote: Request access and we connect the model to your account.

scenarios.title: Split dense housing into houses
scenarios.short: Terraced and tightly packed blocks divided into individual houses.
scenarios.long: Segments dense building blocks as a whole, then divides each block into individual houses from roof markers, using a grid or Voronoi split.
scenarios.output: Individual house polygons within dense blocks.
scenarios.best: High-resolution imagery of terraced or densely built areas.
uses: Count dwellings in dense urban areas
Support census and address mapping
Plan services in informal settlements
scenarios.costNote: Request access and we connect the model to your account.

scenarios.title: Segment anything by zoom
scenarios.short: Universal segmentation. The zoom level decides what you get.
scenarios.long: Zoom 14 outlines land use, large fields and water; zoom 16 small fields and large buildings; zoom 18 farms and groups of trees; zoom 19 and up houses, trees and vehicles.
scenarios.output: Polygons of whatever stands out at the chosen zoom.
scenarios.best: Any RGB imagery. Choose the zoom in the run form.
uses: Outline objects no standard model covers
Pre-segment imagery for manual labelling
Explore a new area before choosing a model
scenarios.costNote: Request access and we connect the model to your account.
